prompt:
Create a final round Minecraft builder reference sheet, landscape 3:2, plain ivory light background, crisp vanilla Minecraft 1.21.1 voxel blocks, skilled human builder quality, no characters or animals. Reference image 1 is the mood/material board; reference image 2 is the previous concept to refine. Keep its successful pale timber, pale stucco, red brick shops, charcoal roof, blue glass, warm lanterns, timber pilings and blue sea-life mosaic.

Layout: two equal columns, LEFT straight-on orthographic elevations viewed from +X east (Alaskan Way), RIGHT matching orthographic three-quarter views from +X and +Z at identical blocks-per-pixel scale. Four aligned rows in order: 0 Pier 59, 1 Bay Wing, 2 Waterfront Landings North, 3 Waterfront Landings South. Each module appears exactly once per column. Clean small labels, abundant space, no large material swatch strip. Show all four complete, with foundations, ground and water where appropriate.

Three essential corrections to previous concept: 1 SITE ORIENTATION AND FOOTPRINT: no generic rectangular plinths or rotating buildings to fit boxes. All geometry stair-steps on the world x/z grid. Pier 59 has a long narrow diagonal footprint running from low-x low-z to high-x high-z across its 120x172 bounding box, with a lobed widened bayward end toward low z; its roof ridge follows that diagonal as a convincing stepped voxel gable. Alaskan Way entrance/sign faces high x. Bay Wing 49x95 is irregular and hooked, with recessed open-water cutouts and narrow connecting decks rather than a solid rectangle. Landings North 66x111 and South 63x103 are deeply U-shaped in plan: long street wing at HIGH X and broad end wings toward LOW X, large open bayward courtyard at LOW X in their middle z range. Show this profound courtyard depth in right views, stepped end wings, recessed balconies, projecting framed bay windows. Do not turn these U shapes sideways. World compass: +X east/uphill, -X Elliott Bay west/downhill, +Z south, -Z north. 2 HEIGHT: use surveyed principal roof heights Pier 59 y26, Bay Wing y18, North y29, South y28, rather than prior exaggerated heights of 39/33/41/40. Limits including terrace fittings 39/33/41/40 respectively. Scale 1.4 blocks/metre. Landings four to six articulated storeys, not merely three repetitive floors. 3 DEPTH AND BUILDABILITY: real stair/slab eaves, verges and ridge; slab floor bands; recessed glass doors; proud bay frames and balconies, stepped roof terraces. Everything stays inside irregular footprint including railings and roof overhangs. Foundations extend to ground, no floating or buried walls. Waterfront terrain mostly rises only 0-3 blocks; pier piles descend to water and seabed. Do not invent a steep hillside beneath these waterfront modules.

Pier 59: long low pale timber historic shed, dark grey gabled roof, restrained skylights, timber deck and railings, exposed piles, modern glass entrance, legible white block lettering 'SEATTLE AQUARIUM' on dark fascia facing +X, cyan/blue sea-life mosaic. Bay Wing: low concrete/glass halls, stepped rooftop blue-water seal and otter pools without animals, viewing terraces and a stair-stepped glass hemisphere underwater-dome hall, railings and accessible stair connections. Landings North and South: related but distinct pale stucco residential masses, red brick ground-floor shops facing +X, teal shop awnings, tall framed bay windows, inset balconies, stepped flat dark roof caps and roof terraces with planters. Warm window lights and lanterns at dusk, blue water with restrained warm reflections. Exterior only, shallow lit shop displays visible through windows.

Exact block palette: birch_planks, birch_stairs, birch_slab for pale timber; smooth_sandstone, smooth_sandstone_stairs, smooth_sandstone_slab for stucco/concrete; bricks, brick_stairs, brick_slab, brick_wall for bases; smooth_quartz, smooth_quartz_stairs, smooth_quartz_slab for trim; deepslate_tiles, deepslate_tile_stairs, deepslate_tile_slab, deepslate_tile_wall for roofs and fascia; light_blue_stained_glass and light_blue_stained_glass_pane for dome, windows and pool viewing walls; dark_oak_log, dark_oak_planks, dark_oak_stairs, dark_oak_slab, dark_oak_fence, dark_oak_trapdoor for piles, decks and framing; iron_bars for rails; lantern, chain, sea_lantern hidden behind glass for warm lit displays; cyan_concrete, blue_concrete, light_blue_concrete, white_concrete for sea-life mosaic and block sign; cyan_wool and cyan_carpet for teal awnings; stone_bricks, stone_brick_stairs, stone_brick_slab for modest ground bases; water; oak_leaves, oak_log, flower_pot, fern, azalea for terrace plants. Use only actual vanilla block shapes, no smooth sculpted domes, no thin non-block architectural geometry, no newer blocks, no custom textures. Render handsome readable architectural reference, not photoreal real buildings.

roles.role: Stucco, aquarium concrete and pool coping
Bay frames, cornices and floor bands
Roof slopes, eaves, ridges and terrace caps
Piles, decking, framing and timber details

changes: Generated with the built-in image tool, inspected, and saved as concept-2.png.
Biggest prior shortfall: generic rectangular massing. This round adds deeper Landings courtyards and more irregular aquarium decks; exact footprint-cell compliance and orientation remain unverified.
Biggest prior shortfall: maximum plot heights presented as building heights. Labels now distinguish surveyed roof levels 26/18/29/28 from height limits; rendered dimensions remain illustrative.
Biggest prior shortfall: shallow, repetitive façades. Projecting bays, recessed balconies, terrace setbacks and framed shop entrances now give stronger depth.
Preserved the pale walls, brick shop bases, charcoal gable, blue glazing, exposed timber piles, aquarium mosaic and warm lighting.

Inspection limitations: the pier row duplicates Bay Wing features, Landings still reads mainly as three storeys, water surrounds the residential bases, and the northeast camera label conflicts with +Z south. The palette is the intended vanilla construction mapping; individual blocks cannot all be verified visually.
